transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen, Marcus Patel, Ravi Singh - Redwood; Emma Ruiz, Jorge Delgado, Samir Khan, Lena Osei - BeaconFold

Topics: onboarding runbook, staging benchmark, network access, KMS/encryption, rollout policy, SLA expectations

00:00 Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you hear me okay?
00:05 Emma: Yup, loud and clear. Thanks Alyssa.
00:08 Jorge: Yep. Good to go.

01:12 Alyssa: Cool. Agenda today, I want to run through the operational playbook we drafted, confirm networking and creds for staging, and set the benchmark window. Marcus will walk through the perf checklist, Ravi will cover adoption milestones.
01:30 Marcus: Hi all, I'll try to keep the deep stuff to the demo part but want to call out two things up front — KV cache priming and continuous batching settings, they matter for your short prompt latencies.
01:45 Samir: Quick question, when you say KV cache priming, are we talking about a pre-warm step on your side or something we need to orchestrate in our infra?
02:10 Marcus: Good call. We can do a mixture — Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching at the serving layer; for benchmarks we usually do a short priming run from your staging VPC so the cache lives in the same AZ. We'll provide the script.

03:01 Lena: From a security/compliance side I want to be sure keys never leave our KMS. How does Redwood handle envelope encryption and HSM?
03:22 Alyssa: Short answer, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations — we have docs to show exact permissions. Marcus, do you want to add the note about audit logs?
03:34 Marcus: Sure — we stream audit events to your Splunk/stack or S3, depending on preference. The runbook we shared includes the log schema. Note sometimes the transcriber turns KMS into K-M-S spelled out — sorry if that shows up weird in docs.

05:00 Emma: Timeline for production — we said Q4 roll, but today we're just confirming staging. Success criteria: lat < 200ms p50 for typical query, cost under $0.006/token effective after batching, and no PII persisted.
05:28 Alyssa: Got it. We'll put those as golden metrics in the playbook. For cost numbers we'll need to confirm token accounting after the run and tuning.

07:15 Marcus: For the staging benchmark I'd like to propose two windows — a 2-hour baseline run with default settings, then a 1-hour tuned run enabling batching and quantization. That helps us compare delta.
07:33 Samir: Sounds fine. We'll need the perf script and temporary creds. I can provision a test role and share the ARN.
07:50 Jorge: On network, do we need to open any inbound rules? We try to avoid inbound openings.
08:02 Marcus: No inbound — we initiate connections from your staging subnet to our ingestion endpoint. We'll need egress to specific Red-wood endpoints and a VPC peering/VPN depending on whether you want private routing.

09:45 Alyssa: Action item: Samir share the VPC CIDR and preferred peering type. Marcus will send the precise endpoint list.

11:20 Lena: One more security nuance — we require per-token audit logs for a week in our retention policy; can Redwood surface token-level logs?
11:38 Marcus: We can surface token-level traces but we usually recommend sampling for cost and privacy; however for compliance we can enable full trace for a defined window and ship it to your S3 under your account.

13:50 Emma: Can you remind us how rollouts are handled? We want canary first then widen if errors stay low.
14:04 Alyssa: Absolutely. Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policy. You can set the percent and error thresholds. Marcus, do you want to call out what metrics drive the fallback?
14:15 Marcus: Sure — latency p95, error rate per 1000 requests, and token generation variance. For model variant fallback we can route to a smaller quantized variant. Sometimes the transcript calls it a "quant variant" — hope that makes sense.

16:40 Samir: On the private deployment option — if we wanted an on-prem package down the line, what's the typical lead time?
16:56 Alyssa: For private on-prem it's several weeks: licensing, network review, and an on-site install if required. But for this pilot we're focused on VPC/private-peering to Redwood hosted.

18:15 Emma: Regarding identities — we'll use SAML SSO for engineers and RBAC for service roles. Do you support attribute-based access for per-team scoping?
18:30 Marcus: Yes, RBAC and SAML mapping to roles is supported. We'll send an example mapping.

20:10 Alyssa: Ok, I'm going to open the live runbook now and walk through the sections so everyone knows where to find things. (links pasted into chat)
20:25 Alyssa: Section one is onboarding checklist, two is network onboarding, three is perf benchmark, four is rollout and monitoring, five is incident playbook.

22:05 Marcus: I'll zoom in on the perf section — pointers: set your max sequence to 1024 for the benchmark, monitor AI GPU memory growth, and if you see high tail latency consider smaller batch sizes. We often mis-transcribe "batch sizes" as "bad sizes" in auto transcripts, ignore that.

24:40 Samir: About cost — batching is great but it can increase p95. Can we do hybrid where we batch for low-latency background tasks only?
24:58 Marcus: You can route by policy. Redwood's smart routing can send low-latency requests to a latency-optimized pool and cost-optimized to a different pool. We'll include a policy example in the runbook.

27:20 Emma: One operational question: who owns tokenization edge cases? If our tokenizer behaves differently will cost estimates be off?
27:36 Marcus: Yes tokenization differences matter; we'll use the same tokenizer for benchmarks. If you have a custom tokenizer we'll add a normalization step in the pipeline.

29:10 Alyssa: Scheduling: agreed to run the two-window benchmark week of 10/26. Marcus to run the scripts against BeaconFold staging. We'll meet after to review results — propose 10/29 for results review.
29:32 Jorge: 10/29 works for us. Emma ok?
29:36 Emma: Yep.

31:00 Lena: For the compliance doc — can we get a redlined copy showing what is covered by Redwood vs what BeaconFold must retain?
31:12 Alyssa: Yes we'll send a responsibilities matrix. Action assigned to Alyssa and Ravi to draft.

33:00 Samir: Small note — we use a few proprietary internal tags in headers, will that break anything?
33:12 Marcus: Usually fine; we'll strip headers we don't need, but we should test. Add that to the staging checklist.

35:40 Marcus: Also, during the tuned run we'll enable quantization profile q4_0 as a test. Expect 15-30% CPU/GPU reduction but watch for small accuracy delta. Emma you'll want to validate eval prompts.
35:58 Emma: Yup we'll run the eval set during the tuned slot.

38:20 Alyssa: Alright, recapping action items and owners (reads list) — Samir provide VPC cidr and role, Marcus send perf scripts, Alyssa share playbook and responsibilities matrix, Lena list compliance blockers.

40:05 Jorge: One more ask — can you include recommended alert thresholds for our PagerDuty?
40:18 Marcus: Yep, we'll include a recommended set: p95 latency > 500ms, error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes, token variance spike.

42:00 Emma: Anything else?
42:06 Alyssa: Not from us. We'll follow-up with the links, runbook, and schedule. Thanks everyone.
42:20 Samir: Thanks all.
42:30 Meeting end.
